capture_blocker.cause: macOS privacy (TCC) permissions, not an application or base-branch defect
evidence: screencapture -x /tmp/probe.png -> 'could not create image from display' (exit 1)
screencapture -x -R 0,0,100,100 -> 'could not create image from rect' (exit 1)
osascript 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process' -> execution error -1743, 'Not authorized to send Apple events to System Events'
capture_blocker.not_a_headless_environment: launchctl managername = Aqua, WindowServer is running, console user is clint. A GUI session exists; the agent's process simply cannot reach it.
capture_blocker.probable_root_cause: The agent runs inside a VS Code tunnel/remote server process (TERM_PROGRAM=vscode, parent chain under ~/.vscode/cli/servers/Stable-*/server). That process has no GUI attribution, so it can hold neither the Screen Recording grant that screencapture needs nor the Automation->System Events grant that window positioning and resizing need. Permissions attach to the responsible process, so nothing spawned from here inherits them either.
required_to_fix: System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording: grant to the terminal/host app that runs the agent
System Settings > Privacy & Security > Automation: allow that same host app to control System Events
Both prompts are interactive and require a human at the machine; they cannot be granted from an unattended run.
capture_blocker.retry_policy: Per the skill's constraints, this was reported rather than retried blindly. screencapture did not produce empty images -- it failed outright, so no amount of retrying would change the result.

seed_rationale: Judgement call, made unattended. Three sites rather than the skill's default two: example.com resolves (Up), down.invalid never resolves so it renders Down without waiting on a real outage, and a third entry with no label exercises render.ts's other branch -- with a label the name cell emits both .site-primary and .site-secondary spans, without one it emits only .site-primary. US4 requires evidence the list renders identically after the SVG deletion, so both name-cell shapes belong in the shot.

views.why: Regression evidence that the removals changed nothing visible: US2 SC-007 (add/edit/check/delete and launch-at-login still work), US3 (window title is still 'Site Checker' after the package/lib rename), US4 FR-005 (no missing-image placeholders once the three scaffold SVGs are deleted).
views.how_to_reach: Launch with the seed_sites above written to sites.json. Wait ~5s after the window appears so rows settle from Pending to Up/Down before capturing.

views.why: The primary changed surface. FR-006/FR-007 reword the parse-error arm of store.rs::load, which today reads 'sites.json could not be read ({e}). Starting with an empty list; the existing file has been left alone.' This is the one view where before/after should visibly differ.
views.how_to_reach: Before launching, write text that is not valid JSON (e.g. 'this is not a site list') to sites.json. The store is read once at startup, so this needs its own app launch. Doubles as the empty-state view: the list is empty, so #empty ('No sites yet. Add one below.') shows beneath the banner.

views.why: FR-006's other half. The I/O-error arm today reads 'Could not read sites.json ({e}). Starting empty.' -- FR-006 requires the two messages not share an opening phrase, so both sides of the comparison need capturing to judge SC-004.
views.how_to_reach: Before launching, write the valid seed then chmod 000 sites.json to force EACCES. Needs its own app launch. Restore with chmod 644 immediately after, before the backup is moved back.
views.note: Lowest priority of the three if a future run needs to economise -- it requires a third app launch and a chmod that must be undone.
